newsitem.title: USA: Silicon Graphics stock jumps after earnings report.
newsitem.headline: Silicon Graphics stock jumps after earnings report.

text.p: The stock of Silicon Graphics Inc. gained 33 percent in value Friday after the computer workstation maker reported surprisingly strong fiscal fourth-quarter earnings.

The Mountain View, Calif.-based company's stock rose $5.94 to $25.75 in composite morning trading on the New York Stock Exchange, where it was the most actively traded issue on volume of more than 3 million shares. Trading in the stock was briefly halted.

The company, whose products are used in computer-intensive applications ranging from complex weather modelling to special effects in movies, issued an earnings report late Thursday that startled Wall Street after nearly two years of quarterly shortfalls.

Silicon Graphics reported net income of $102 million, or 56 cents a share, on sales of $1.2 billion. A year earlier, the company posted a loss of $48.7 million, or 30 cents a share, on sales of $977 million.

The profit, announced after the close of market trading, easily beat the 34 cents a share that Wall Street analysts surveyed by First Call had expected. In after-hours trading, its stock jumped to $24.50.

In addition, Chief Executive Officer Edward McCracken said in an interview Thursday that he expects Silicon Graphics to be able to sustain the higher profit margins it achieved in the latest quarter throughout its 1998 fiscal year.
Bear Stearns upped its rating for Silicon Graphics stock to attractive from neutral.

The favourable earnings report gave Silicon Graphics investors a welcome boost after a sweeping product transition over the last year had battered the shares and contributed to repeated earnings disappointments.

"This quarter was all about execution," McCracken said. "Our product transition is complete, we are shipping our entire product line ... and, most importantly, the new products are finding strong acceptance with customers."

The fourth-quarter result included pre-tax merger charges of $6 million related to the company's April 1996 acquisition of supercomputer maker Cray Research. That compared with charges of $120 million in the same quarter a year earlier related to the same transaction.

McCracken said the fourth quarter was the last in which the company will report charges related to the Cray acquisition, although it will write off around $20 million in the current quarter related to acquisition of a 3-D Internet software firm.
For the year, Silicon Graphics earned $78.5 million, or 43 cents a share, on sales of $3.09 billion. A year earlier, the company earned $115 million, or 65 cents a share, on sales of $2.55 billion.
